title: Initial ridge-spur lake-road shore endpoint arrangement
scope: Qualitative upper-shore staging and seasonal-spur arrangement for the established lake road; exact placement, mapping, engineering, infrastructure, transport, staffing, shore use, ecological overlap, safety, and guaranteed access remain open.
approval_evidence: On 2026-08-15 the Author replied, 'I choose B — Upper-shore staging + seasonal spurs for the lake-road shore endpoint.'
question: What qualitative shore-endpoint arrangement should govern how the established lake road meets the changeable lake margin without fixing exact placement, engineering, infrastructure, transport, staffing, ecological use, safety, or guaranteed access?
selection: Use B — Upper-shore staging + seasonal spurs. The road ends at one recurring upper-shore staging place on relatively firm ground set back from the ordinarily shifting wet margin. Several short seasonal spurs extend toward nearby shore contacts. Which contact is usable, and therefore which spur can serve as the final approach, can vary with seasonal and local conditions, so the staging place recurs while the final shore contact can change. The staging place and any spur can flood, erode, ice over, attract wildlife, or become unusable; these are possible impairments rather than selected events or access guarantees.
alternatives: A — Single shore work point: The road reaches one maintained working point at the water’s edge. It becomes the strongest recurring landmark and concentrates loading and upkeep, but trouble there disrupts most routine access and human pressure stays focused on one shore. Commits us to one primary shore terminal. It still creates no dock, boats, buildings, permanent staff, harbour, or all-season access. Not selected.

B — Upper-shore staging + seasonal spurs: The road ends on relatively firm ground set back from the ordinarily shifting wet margin. Several short seasonal spurs lead to whichever nearby shore contacts are usable, so the staging place recurs while the final alien shoreline changes. Best balance of haulage and seasonal ecology. The staging place and every spur can still flood, erode, ice over, attract wildlife, or become unusable. Selected.

C — Dispersed seasonal access: The constructed road ends at a general lakeward approach. People continue along informal or lightly reused paths chosen for current conditions, producing the wildest shore experience but the weakest logistical anchor for a laden return. Lowest fixed infrastructure; highest route-finding, carrying, and dispersed exposure. Informal does not mean random, unknown, or culturally unregulated. Not selected.
rationale: The selected arrangement preserves a recurring upper-shore landmark for later route and haulage development while allowing the final approach to follow a seasonally changing alien wet margin. It does so without selecting a water-edge terminal, dock, boat, building, permanent worker, shore settlement, defensive post, or all-season access.
evidence: Author selection on 2026-08-15: 'I choose B — Upper-shore staging + seasonal spurs for the lake-road shore endpoint.'
consequences: The established lake road ends at one recurring upper-shore staging place.
The staging place is on relatively firm ground set back from the ordinarily shifting wet margin.
Several short seasonal spurs extend from the staging place toward nearby shore contacts.
Which contact is usable, and therefore which spur can serve as the final approach, can vary with seasonal and local conditions.
The staging place recurs while the final shore contact can change.

Upper-shore, relatively firm, set back, ordinarily shifting, several, short, seasonal, nearby, usable, staging place, and shore contact are qualitative author-facing relations; short is relative to the main lake road.
Seasonal use establishes no calendar, fixed rotation, one-spur-per-season pattern, or proof that water level is the only selection cue.

The staging place and any spur can flood, erode, ice over, attract wildlife, or become unusable; no particular impairment, closure, damage, wildlife presence, repair, bypass, or incident is established.
Several spurs do not guarantee that any usable shore contact exists at a particular time.
Relative firmness and setback create no surveyed flood line, pavement, engineering, load rating, dryness, stability, safety, maintenance, view, or operational guarantee.

WLD-LOCATION-002 remains the sole authority for its broad fair-weather whole-journey bands; this decision creates no staging-to-shore band and does not partition, extend, shorten, or recalculate either accepted anchor.

No dock, ramp, bridge, causeway, boat, vehicle, building, cache, storage, processing, staffing, ownership, toll, access rule, maintenance authority, trade, defence, institution, or lakeshore settlement is selected.
WLD-ECOLOGY-004 and WLD-ECOLOGY-006 remain contextual authorities; no spur is assigned to a crown-herd path, nursery, migration route, fishery, predator concentration, harvest site, or other habitat.
The arrangement is author-side spatial truth and does not become automatic character knowledge of current ground, water, ice, wildlife, access, or future condition.
Ordinary finite land, matter, energy, labour, time, carriage, maintenance, obstruction, and recovery remain causal.

No inventory rule, encumbrance formula, travel calculation, movement modifier, route readout, map revelation, pathfinding effect, fast travel, teleportation, safe zone, automatic repair, spawn, reset, reward, free resource, or guaranteed recovery is created.
